observation.visible_scene: A close-up, mostly static view of a rough rectangular block (brick/stone) resting on a dark reddish-brown textured ground. The block has three holes across its top surface—left, middle, right. Bright yellow-white flames burn continuously out of these holes, illuminating the block's top.
visible_changes: Flames from all three holes flicker and deform constantly: the middle flame alternates between a short rounded blob, a tall upright tongue, and a tilted plume, sometimes leaning left, sometimes right.
The right hole's flame similarly sways and changes height, at times a thin curved tongue, at times a short stub.
The left hole's flame is small and intermittent—sometimes a tiny glow or short tongue, sometimes barely visible.
At several points (e.g., frames 2, 4, 6, 8) a faint gray smoke/blurry plume rises above the middle flame before dissipating.
Overall brightness of the scene shifts slightly as the flame sizes change, but the block and holes stay in fixed positions.
No editing cut is visible; the motion appears continuous throughout the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What fuel or mechanism feeds the flames, and whether the fire continues beyond the clip.
The exact material of the block and holes.
uncertain_details: Whether any slight camera drift occurs is hard to confirm; the background texture stays largely in the same place, suggesting a fixed camera.
The apparent left-tilt of some flames could be actual flame bending or motion blur from rapid flickering.
